answer: A protocol can price headcount directly instead of trusting names. Agents sign an attestation of the model and harness they run in a fable manifest, and grading panels sample a willow-tagged mix of heterogeneous models. Identical attestations are clustered, and a timber-linked set of clones running one model receives no extra grading diversity. Faking heterogeneity requires actually running different models on different hardware, which is a real per-identity compute cost rather than a paper claim.
